title: Stars and Bars: Weak Compositions of n into k Parts Number C(n+k−1, n)
description: A weak composition of n into k parts is a function f : Fin k → ℕ whose values sum to n (parts may be zero, hence 'weak'). The stars-and-bars theorem counts them: card {f : Fin k → ℕ // ∑ i, f i = n} = C(n + k − 1, n). The mnemonic lays n stars in a row and inserts k−1 bars to split them into k (possibly empty) groups; arranging n stars and k−1 bars in a line is a choice of n positions among n + (k−1), giving C(n + k − 1, n). This entry formalises the function/tuple form of the count. Mathlib proves only the multiset form Sym.card_sym_eq_choose : card (Sym α k) = C(card α + k − 1, k); it does not record the equivalent and more familiar tuple statement. The gap is the explicit bijection weakCompositionEquivSym : {f : Fin k → ℕ // ∑ i, f i = n} ≃ Sym (Fin k) n, which sends a weak composition to the multiset containing index i with multiplicity f i, with inverse sending a multiset s to the multiplicity function i ↦ Multiset.count i s. The forward direction has the right size because card (∑ i, replicate (f i) i) = ∑ i, f i = n (Multiset.card_sum, card_replicate); the inverse has the right sum because ∑ i, count i s = card s = n (Multiset.sum_count_eq_card). The two are mutually inverse by Multiset.count_sum' + count_replicate + Fintype.sum_ite_eq' one way and Multiset.toFinset_sum_count_nsmul_eq the other. A Fintype instance for the weak-composition subtype (which is not auto-derivable, since the codomain ℕ is infinite) is supplied through the bijection, after which card_weakComposition reads off C(n + k − 1, n) from Sym.card_sym_eq_choose and Fintype.card_fin.

meta.author: Researcher agent (lean-genius), formalized in Lean 4 over Mathlib

relatedProblems.relationship: Sibling enumerative count for the ordered-tuple model: that entry counts compositions of n into exactly k POSITIVE parts as C(n−1, k−1) via a cuts-in-gaps bijection. This entry counts WEAK compositions (parts may be zero) as C(n+k−1, n) via a bijection to multisets. The two stars-and-bars variants — bars between vs. bars among stars — differ exactly by whether empty parts are allowed.
Grandparent of the positive-parts count; both turn a Mathlib cardinality fact into a named closed-form enumeration graded by a structural parameter.

meta.assumptions: 0 axioms, 0 sorries, no native_decide. All three named theorems (count_toMultiset, card_toMultiset, card_weakComposition) and the bijection weakCompositionEquivSym were verified with #print axioms to depend only on the foundational propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound. Mathlib records only the multiset form of stars and bars (Sym.card_sym_eq_choose); the function/tuple form C(n+k−1, n) and the bijection weakCompositionEquivSym to Sym (Fin k) n are the original content here. The Fintype instance on the weak-composition subtype is supplied through that bijection (it is not auto-derivable because the codomain ℕ is infinite). The result is unconditional for all k, n ≥ 0.

overview.historicalContext: Stars and bars is one of the foundational counting principles of enumerative combinatorics, usually attributed to William Feller. The question — in how many ways can n indistinguishable balls be placed into k distinguishable boxes — is the same as counting the nonnegative integer solutions of x₁ + ⋯ + x_k = n. The picture that names the method: draw the n balls as stars in a row and separate them into k groups with k−1 bars; every arrangement of n stars and k−1 bars in a line is one solution, and there are C(n + k − 1, n) ways to choose which n of the n + (k−1) symbols are stars. The same count answers 'how many multisets of size n can be drawn from a k-element alphabet' — the multichoose number — and it is the weak (parts allowed to be zero) counterpart of the count of ordered positive compositions, C(n−1, k−1).
overview.problemStatement:
Show that the number of weak compositions of n into k parts — functions f : Fin k → ℕ with ∑ᵢ f(i) = n — is the binomial coefficient

$$\#\{f : \mathrm{Fin}\ k \to \mathbb{N} \mid \textstyle\sum_i f(i) = n\} = \binom{n + k - 1}{n}.$$

Equivalently, the number of nonnegative integer solutions of x₁ + ⋯ + x_k = n is C(n + k − 1, n).
overview.text: Mathlib proves the multiset form of stars and bars, Sym.card_sym_eq_choose : card (Sym α k) = C(card α + k − 1, k), counting size-k multisets over a finite alphabet α. It does not record the equivalent function/tuple form, that the number of ℕ-valued tuples on k indices summing to n is C(n + k − 1, n). Both are supplied here. The bridge is the bijection weakCompositionEquivSym : {f : Fin k → ℕ // ∑ i, f i = n} ≃ Sym (Fin k) n, identifying a weak composition with the size-n multiset over the index set Fin k that contains each index i with multiplicity f(i).
overview.proofStrategy: The forward map sends a weak composition f to the multiset toMultiset f = ∑ i, Multiset.replicate (f i) i. Its size is correct because Multiset.card distributes over the Finset sum (Multiset.card_sum) and card (replicate (f i) i) = f i (Multiset.card_replicate), so card (toMultiset f) = ∑ i, f i = n (card_toMultiset). The inverse sends a multiset s to the multiplicity function i ↦ Multiset.count i s; its values sum to n because ∑ i, count i s = card s = n over a Fintype index (Multiset.sum_count_eq_card). The two maps are mutually inverse: count j (toMultiset f) = ∑ i, count j (replicate (f i) i) = ∑ i, (if i = j then f i else 0) = f j (Multiset.count_sum', Multiset.count_replicate, Fintype.sum_ite_eq' — this is count_toMultiset); and ∑ i, replicate (count i s) i = ∑ i, count i s • {i} = ∑_{i ∈ s.toFinset} count i s • {i} = s, extending the universal sum to the support sum (terms outside the support vanish since their count is 0) and closing with Multiset.toFinset_sum_count_nsmul_eq. A Fintype instance on the subtype is then obtained by Fintype.ofEquiv from this bijection — necessary because Lean cannot synthesise Fintype {f : Fin k → ℕ // …} directly (the codomain ℕ is infinite). Finally card_weakComposition transports the cardinality through Fintype.card_congr and applies Sym.card_sym_eq_choose with card (Fin k) = k (Fintype.card_fin), giving C(k + n − 1, n) = C(n + k − 1, n).
keyInsights: **A weak composition is literally a multiset of indices**: the function f : Fin k → ℕ and the multiset ∑ i, replicate (f i) i carry the same information — f records the multiplicity of each index, and Multiset.count recovers it. This is the precise statement that 'choosing how many of each of k types' is 'choosing a size-n multiset over k types', and it is what makes the count the multichoose number C(n+k−1, n).

**The two roundtrips are exactly Mathlib's count/replicate calculus**: one direction is count_sum' + count_replicate collapsing to a single nonzero term (Fintype.sum_ite_eq'); the other is the standard fact that a multiset is the sum over its support of count-many copies of each element (toFinset_sum_count_nsmul_eq), with the universal sum reduced to the support sum because absent elements have count 0.

**Weak vs. positive is empty-parts-allowed**: this C(n+k−1, n) count is the sibling of the positive-parts count C(n−1, k−1) for ordered compositions; the difference is solely whether the parts may be zero, which is the difference between bars placed among the stars and bars placed in the gaps between stars.

**Mathlib stops at the multiset form**: Sym.card_sym_eq_choose is available, but the tuple/function form and the bijection to it are not in Mathlib; that bijection is the original content of this entry. A consequence is that the Fintype instance on the summing subtype must itself be built from the bijection.
prerequisites: Multisets over a finite type: Multiset.count, Multiset.replicate, and the count/replicate calculus (count_replicate, count_sum', card_sum, card_replicate)
The fact that a multiset equals the support-sum of count-many copies of each element (Multiset.toFinset_sum_count_nsmul_eq) and that counts sum to the cardinality (Multiset.sum_count_eq_card)
Mathlib's symmetric-power type Sym α n = {s : Multiset α // card s = n} and the multiset stars-and-bars count Sym.card_sym_eq_choose
Transporting cardinality along a bijection (Fintype.card_congr) and building a Fintype instance from an equivalence (Fintype.ofEquiv)

sections.title: The Stars-and-Bars Principle and the Mathlib Gap
sections.mathContext: $\#\{f : \mathrm{Fin}\ k \to \mathbb{N} \mid \sum_i f(i) = n\} = \binom{n + k - 1}{n}$, the multichoose count.
sections.summary: The module docstring fixes the object of study (weak compositions f : Fin k → ℕ with ∑ᵢ f(i) = n, parts allowed to be zero), states the headline count C(n+k−1, n) with the stars-and-bars mnemonic that names it, and lays out the bijective plan: a weak composition is the same data as a size-n multiset over Fin k. It records the precise Mathlib gap — Mathlib has the multiset form Sym.card_sym_eq_choose but never the function/tuple form — which is the content this entry contributes.

sections.title: The Multiset Attached to a Weak Composition
sections.mathContext: $\mathrm{toMultiset}\ f = \sum_i \mathrm{replicate}\,(f(i))\,i$, with $\mathrm{count}_j(\mathrm{toMultiset}\ f) = f(j)$ and $\#(\mathrm{toMultiset}\ f) = \sum_i f(i)$.
sections.summary: toMultiset packages a weak composition f : Fin k → ℕ as the multiset over Fin k in which index i occurs f(i) times. Two bookkeeping lemmas pin it down: count_toMultiset shows recovering the multiplicity of j returns f(j) (Multiset.count_sum' splits the count over the Finset sum, count_replicate makes each summand an indicator, and Fintype.sum_ite_eq' collapses to f(j)); card_toMultiset shows its size is ∑ i, f(i) (Multiset.card_sum distributes card over the sum, card_replicate evaluates each term).

sections.title: The Bijection to Size-n Multisets
sections.summary: weakCompositionEquivSym is the explicit equivalence: forward, f ↦ toMultiset f (size n by card_toMultiset); backward, s ↦ (i ↦ count i s) (sum n by Multiset.sum_count_eq_card). left_inv is count_toMultiset applied pointwise; right_inv is the identity ∑ i, replicate (count i s) i = s, obtained by rewriting replicate as count i s • {i} (nsmul_singleton), shrinking the universal sum to the support sum (absent indices have count 0), and applying Multiset.toFinset_sum_count_nsmul_eq.

sections.title: Finiteness Transported Across the Bijection
sections.mathContext: $\mathrm{Fintype}\,\{f : \mathrm{Fin}\ k \to \mathbb{N} \mid \sum_i f(i) = n\}$ via $\mathrm{Fintype.ofEquiv}\,(\mathrm{Sym}\,(\mathrm{Fin}\ k)\ n)$.
sections.summary: instFintypeWeakComposition supplies the Fintype instance on the summing subtype by Fintype.ofEquiv through weakCompositionEquivSym. It is genuinely necessary: Lean cannot synthesise a Fintype for a subtype of Fin k → ℕ on its own, because the codomain ℕ is infinite, so the bijection to the manifestly finite Sym (Fin k) n is the certificate of finiteness — and only with this instance in scope does the headline Fintype.card statement typecheck.

sections.title: The Count C(n+k−1, n)
sections.summary: card_weakComposition is the headline result. Fintype.card_congr transports the cardinality along weakCompositionEquivSym to card (Sym (Fin k) n), which Sym.card_sym_eq_choose evaluates to C(card (Fin k) + n − 1, n); with Fintype.card_fin and commutativity of addition this is C(n + k − 1, n).

conclusion.summary: The function/tuple form of stars and bars — weak compositions of n into k parts number C(n + k − 1, n) — is formalised sorry-free and axiom-free. The mathematical content beyond Mathlib is the explicit bijection weakCompositionEquivSym between the summing subtype {f : Fin k → ℕ // ∑ i, f i = n} and the symmetric power Sym (Fin k) n, identifying a weak composition with the multiset of its indices counted with multiplicity. Mathlib records only the multiset form Sym.card_sym_eq_choose; this entry supplies the equivalent and more familiar tuple count, together with the Fintype instance on the summing subtype that the bijection makes available. It is the weak (empty-parts-allowed) sibling of the positive-parts composition count C(n−1, k−1).
conclusion.implications: Because the result is delivered as an explicit Equiv (not merely a cardinality equation), it is reusable: any downstream count phrased as 'ℕ-valued tuples on k indices summing to n' can now be rewritten as a multiset count over Fin k, and the Fintype instance on the summing subtype unlocks Finset.sum / Fintype.card reasoning over weak compositions elsewhere. The bijective, axiom-free style also makes the entry a candidate for upstreaming the tuple form to Mathlib, which currently stops at Sym.card_sym_eq_choose.
openQuestions: Formalize the generating-function view: ∑ₙ (#weak compositions of n into k parts) xⁿ = 1/(1−x)ᵏ, recovering C(n+k−1,n) as the coefficient and connecting to the negative-binomial series.

Prove the bounded-parts refinement — weak compositions of n into k parts each at most m — counted by inclusion–exclusion ∑ⱼ (−1)ʲ C(k,j) C(n−j(m+1)+k−1, k−1), of which the unbounded count here is the m→∞ case.
Establish the symmetry/duality with the positive-parts count C(n−1,k−1) as an explicit bijection (add 1 to each part), unifying the two stars-and-bars variants formalized across the sibling entries.
